name: Heart & Circulation
summary: The pump that moves blood around your body.

lessons.title: Four chambers
lessons.body: The heart is a muscular organ about the size of a fist. It has four chambers. The two upper chambers, the right and left atria, receive blood. The two lower chambers, the right and left ventricles, pump blood out. A wall called the septum separates the right side from the left side.
keyPoints: Atria receive blood; ventricles pump it out
The septum divides the right and left sides
The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood to the whole body

lessons.title: The four valves
lessons.body: Valves keep blood flowing in one direction. The tricuspid valve sits between the right atrium and right ventricle. The pulmonary valve lies between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery. The mitral valve (also called the bicuspid valve) sits between the left atrium and left ventricle. The aortic valve lies between the left ventricle and the aorta.
keyPoints: Tricuspid: right atrium to right ventricle
Pulmonary: right ventricle to pulmonary artery
Mitral: left atrium to left ventricle

lessons.title: Path of blood through the heart
lessons.body: Oxygen-poor blood returns from the body through the vena cava into the right atrium. It passes through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, then through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary artery, which carries it to the lungs. Oxygen-rich blood returns through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium, passes the mitral valve into the left ventricle, and is pumped through the aortic valve into the aorta to the body.
keyPoints: Body to vena cava to right atrium to right ventricle to lungs
Lungs to pulmonary veins to left atrium to left ventricle to aorta to body
Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood toward it

quiz.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
quiz.explanation: The heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles.

quiz.question: Which chamber pumps oxygen-rich blood to the whole body?
quiz.explanation: The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta and around the body.

quiz.question: Which valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle?
quiz.explanation: The mitral (bicuspid) valve sits between the left atrium and left ventricle.

quiz.question: Which vessel carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs?
quiz.explanation: The pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

quiz.question: Why is the left ventricle wall the thickest?
options: It pumps blood to the entire body
quiz.explanation: It must generate enough pressure to push blood around the whole body.

quiz.question: What is the main job of heart valves?
options: Keep blood flowing in one direction
quiz.explanation: Valves open and close to prevent blood from flowing backward.

quiz.question: Which vessels bring oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the heart?
quiz.explanation: The pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

quiz.question: What separates the right and left sides of the heart?
quiz.explanation: The septum is the muscular wall between the two sides.
